target_customer: Quantitative traders and organisations needing event forecasts such as supply chain, energy and earthquake risk
problem: Quant models are built by hand for narrow domains with heavy feature and architecture work; Zoa wants automated, general forecasting models.
business_model: Proprietary forecasting models, currently used for trading; selling models for other domains is a stated aim

founders.name: Sam Damashek
prior_employers: Jane Street (3 years, options trading desk, New York and Hong Kong)
education: Carnegie Mellon University, BS Computer Science

technical_complexity.rationale: Uses LLMs in multi-agent optimisation loops to automate model building for sample-efficient general forecasters, which is research-level work.

defensibility.rationale: Value sits in trained models and trading results which are private; no moat evidence in sources.

market_need_then: Quant and risk teams spend heavy manual effort on narrow models (company site); no independent demand evidence found.

branding.domain_note: Uses zoaresearch.com, a suffixed name form

identity.voice_and_tone: Research lab; claims first profitable AI lab (company claim)

branding.brand_signature: $10,000 grant program for ML research per aggregator

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; confused with ZOA Robotics and other Zoa entities in search.

outcome_analysis: Zoa Research is active with a team of five and claims profitability from trading use, but no funding, revenue or customer data was verified. The founders pair a Jane Street quant with a Harvard Law trained CEO. Outcome cannot be assessed from public sources.
notes: Only aggregator says $500K total raised at seed (unverified, not a round). Two competitor searches returned no dated startups. The profitability claim is the company's own. A search result suggested Zoa also ran a $10,000 research grant program, from a secondary profile.
